qs.stem: A cyclist rides to a studio at 40 km/h and returns by the same road at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, not the average of the two speeds.
Take the one-way distance as 120 km (a number both speeds divide).
Average = 48 km/h.
qs.trap: Taking (40 + 60) ÷ 2 = 50. More time is spent at the slower speed.

qs.stem: A booklet has pages numbered 1 to 99. How many digits are printed in all to number the pages?
steps: Group the pages by how many digits their numbers have.
Total = 189.
qs.trap: Counting pages instead of digits.

qs.stem: Poles are placed every 6 m along the boundary of a rectangular garden 30 m by 24 m, with one pole at each corner. How many poles are needed?
steps: Perimeter = 2 × (30 + 24) = 108 m.
Around a closed loop, the number of poles equals the number of gaps.
Answer: 18 poles.
qs.trap: Adding 1 as you would for a straight line. A closed loop has as many poles as gaps.

qs.stem: A 45-litre mix has paint and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 1 : 1?
steps: Paint = 45 × 3/5 = 27 L; water = 18 L.
Paint does not change. For 1 : 1, water must be 27 × 1/1 = 27 L.
Water to add = 27 − 18 = 9 L.
Answer: 9.
qs.trap: Changing both parts. Only the water increases; the paint stays the same.

qs.stem: What number comes next? 3, 22, 7, 19, 11, ?
steps: Look at the gaps between terms first; if they do not settle, try multiplying, squares, or two series taking turns.
Two series alternate: 3, 7, 11 (+4) and 22, 19, 16 (-3).
Next term: 16.

steps: To reach step k, the last move came from step k − 1 or step k − 2, so ways(k) = ways(k − 1) + ways(k − 2).
ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2.

Gear 4
Gear 6
steps: Gear 1 turns clockwise (red arrow).
Rules: meshing gears turn opposite ways; an open belt keeps the same direction; a crossed belt reverses the direction.
Links: 1→2: cross (reverses), 2→3: mesh (reverses), 3→4: mesh (reverses), 4→5: mesh (reverses), 5→6: mesh (reverses).
Directions: 1 C, 2 A, 3 C, 4 A, 5 C, 6 A (C = clockwise). So the anticlockwise gears are gear 2, gear 4, gear 6.

qs.stem: Which statements about the Moon are true?
opts: Moon phases are caused by the Earth's shadow
It shines by reflecting sunlight
The same side always faces the Earth
Its phases depend on its position relative to the Sun and Earth
steps: The Moon has no light of its own; it reflects sunlight.
It spins once for every trip around Earth, so one face always points to us.
As it orbits, we see different parts of its sunlit half: the phases.
So only "produces its own light" is false.

Correct: It shines by reflecting sunlight; The same side always faces the Earth; Its phases depend on its position relative to the Sun and Earth. Not correct: Moon phases are caused by the Earth's shadow.
qs.trap: Thinking phases are caused by Earth's shadow. That is a lunar eclipse.

qs.stem: A vacuum flask keeps a cold drink cold for hours. Which features help?
opts: A vacuum gap between the inner and outer walls
A black outer surface
A tight stopper
Shiny, silvered inner walls
steps: Heat moves by conduction, convection and radiation.
The vacuum stops conduction and convection between the walls.
Silvered walls reflect radiated heat; the stopper stops air moving in and out.
A black surface absorbs and gives out radiation more, so it does not help.
Correct: A vacuum gap between the inner and outer walls; A tight stopper; Shiny, silvered inner walls. Not correct: A black outer surface.
qs.trap: Choosing the black surface. Black is good at absorbing heat, not blocking it.

opts: Arial
Helvetica
Times New Roman
Futura
steps: Sans-serif typefaces have no small finishing strokes.
Helvetica, Arial and Futura are well-known sans-serifs.
Times New Roman and Garamond are serif typefaces.
So Helvetica, Arial and Futura are correct.
Correct: Arial; Helvetica; Futura. Not correct: Times New Roman.
qs.trap: Choosing Times New Roman because it is common on screens.

qs.stem: What colour do you get when red light and green light overlap on a white wall?
opts: Purple
Brown
Black
Yellow
steps: Light adds together (additive mixing).
Red + green light = yellow.
Red + blue = magenta; green + blue = cyan.
Mixing red and green paint would give a muddy brown, which is why people often get this wrong. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Answering brown: that is what paints do, not light.

qs.stem: Which artist illustrated the pages of the original handwritten Constitution of India?
opts: M. F. Husain
Amrita Sher-Gil
Raja Ravi Varma
Nandalal Bose and his students from Santiniketan
steps: The original Constitution was handwritten in calligraphy.
Its pages were decorated by Nandalal Bose with artists from Kala Bhavana, Santiniketan.
The others were famous painters but did not illustrate it.
Answer: Nandalal Bose and his students. That is option D.
qs.trap: Choosing Ravi Varma, who died decades earlier, in 1906.

qs.stem: Why does the clear sky look blue during the day?
opts: Water vapour absorbs all other colours
The sky reflects the colour of the oceans
Sunlight contains only blue light
Air molecules scatter blue light from the Sun more than red light
steps: Sunlight contains all colours.
Tiny air molecules scatter short (blue) wavelengths much more than long (red) ones.
This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every part of the sky.
At sunset the light passes through more air, so more blue is scattered away and the sky looks red. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Choosing the ocean reflection. The sky is blue even over deserts.

opts: Proximity
Continuity of colour
Similarity
Closure

Proximity is grouping things that are close; similarity is grouping things that look alike.
Many logos use closure to look lighter and more interesting. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Choosing proximity, which is about spacing.

opts: Abanindranath Tagore
Raja Ravi Varma
Jamini Roy
S. H. Raza
steps: Raja Ravi Varma painted scenes from Indian epics in oil.
In 1894 he set up a lithographic press to print affordable copies.
These prints spread widely into homes across India.
Answer: Raja Ravi Varma. That is option B.
qs.trap: Choosing Jamini Roy, who also wanted affordable art but used folk styles.

qs.stem: Two plane mirrors are hinged together at an angle of 90°. A small toy is placed between them. How many images of the toy can be seen?
steps: For two mirrors at angle θ, the number of images is 360 ÷ θ − 1 (when 360 ÷ θ is a whole number and the object sits symmetrically).
Images = 4 − 1 = 3.
At 90° you see 3 images, which you can check with two mirrors at home.
qs.trap: Forgetting to subtract 1: the toy itself is one of the 360 ÷ θ positions.

qs.stem: Five friends compare how old they are. Jaya is older than Divya. Gaurav is older than Divya. Divya is older than Eshan. Divya is older than Aarav. Who is the third oldest?
opts: Divya
Eshan
Gaurav
Aarav
steps: Write each clue as an arrow from the bigger to the smaller.
Combine the arrows to build the order from most to least.
The clues fix position 3: in every order that fits, Divya is there.
So the third oldest is Divya.
qs.trap: Reading one clue backwards. "A is older than B" puts A above B.

qs.stem: Why do railway tracks have small gaps between rail sections?
opts: To make trains easier to steer
To reduce the weight of the track
To leave room for the rails to expand on hot days
To drain rain water
steps: Metals expand when heated.
A long rail grows by several millimetres on a hot day.
Without gaps, the rails would push against each other and buckle.
Many modern tracks are welded and pre-stressed instead. (Option C.)
qs.trap: Choosing drainage. The gaps are about thermal expansion.

qs.stem: In a code language, SKETCH is written as UMGVEJ. How is GALLERY written in the same code?
opts: JDOOHUB
EYJJCPW
ICNNGTA
ATGNNCI
steps: Compare letter by letter: S → U, K → M.
Each letter moves 2 places forward in the alphabet (Z wraps to A).
Apply it to GALLERY: G→I, A→C, L→N, L→N, E→G, R→T, Y→A.
Answer: ICNNGTA.
qs.trap: Shifting in the wrong direction. Check the rule on two letters before applying it.

qs.stem: Through which of these does sound travel fastest?
opts: Air
A steel rail
Water
A vacuum
steps: Sound is a vibration passed from particle to particle.
Particles are packed most tightly and strongly bonded in solids.
Roughly: air 340 m/s, water 1500 m/s, steel about 5000 m/s.
Sound cannot travel through a vacuum at all. (Option B.)
qs.trap: Choosing air because we usually hear sound through it.

qs.stem: In a certain leap year, 1 January is a Tuesday. What day of the week is 20 June in that year?
opts: Thursday
Wednesday
Monday
Friday
steps: Days from 1 January to 20 June: 31 + 29 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 19 = 171.
171 = 7 × 24 + 3, so the weekday moves on by 3.
Tuesday + 3 days = Friday.
Answer: Friday.
qs.trap: Counting 1 January itself as a day to move on. Start from day 0. Also remember February has 29 days in a leap year.

qs.stem: What comes next in the series: D, F, I, M, R, ?
opts: X
W
Y
Z
steps: Turn letters into positions: D=4, F=6, I=9, M=13, R=18.
Gaps: +2, +3, +4, +5, growing by 1 each time.
Next gap: +6, so 18 + 6 = 24 = X.
Answer: X.
qs.trap: Counting the gap by including the starting letter. Use letter positions.
